```{r}
library(tidyquant)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(scales)
library(gridExtra)

Diamond <- read_csv("diamonds.csv")
Diamond$cut     <- factor(Diamond$cut,     levels = c("Fair","Good","Very Good","Premium","Ideal"))
Diamond$color   <- factor(Diamond$color,   levels = c("J","I","H","G","F","E","D"))
Diamond$clarity <- factor(Diamond$clarity, levels = c("I1","SI2","SI1","VS2","VS1","VVS2","VVS1","IF"))

# 1. Price distribution (raw vs log) --------------------------------------
p1 <- ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = price)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 80, fill = "#2C7BB6", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(title = "Figure 1A: Price Distribution (Level)", x = "Price (USD)", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

p2 <- ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = log(price))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 80, fill = "#D7191C", color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Figure 1B: Price Distribution (Log-Transformed)", x = "ln(Price)", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

grid.arrange(p1, p2, ncol = 2)

# 2. Carat vs Price — the main relationship + log scale ------------------
p3 <- ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = carat, y = price)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.08, color = "#2C7BB6", size = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "#D7191C", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  labs(title = "Figure 2A: Transaction Price vs. Carat Weight", x = "Carat Weight", y = "Price (USD)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

p4 <- ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = log(carat), y = log(price))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.08, color = "#2C7BB6", size = 0.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#D7191C", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Figure 2B: Log-Price vs. Log-Carat Weight", x = "ln(Carat Weight)", y = "ln(Price)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

grid.arrange(p3, p4, ncol = 2)

# 3. Psychological thresholds — density near round carat numbers ----------
Diamond_sub <- Diamond %>% filter(carat >= 0.8, carat <= 2.2)

ggplot(Diamond_sub, aes(x = carat)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.01, fill = "#2C7BB6", color = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(1.0, 1.5, 2.0), color = "#D7191C", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  annotate("text", x = c(1.02, 1.52, 2.02), y = Inf, label = c("1.0ct", "1.5ct", "2.0ct"), hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, color = "#D7191C", size = 3.5) +
  labs(title = "Figure 3: Density of Carat Weights Near Psychological Thresholds", x = "Carat Weight", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)

# 4. Boxplots: price by each categorical variable -------------------------
p5 <- ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = cut, y = price, fill = cut)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Blues") +
  labs(title = "Figure 4A: Price Distribution by Cut Grade", x = NULL, y = "Price (USD)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")

p6 <- ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = color, y = price, fill = color)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Oranges") +
  labs(title = "Figure 4B: Price Distribution by Color Grade", x = NULL, y = "Price (USD)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")

p7 <- ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = clarity, y = price, fill = clarity)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.size = 0.3, outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Greens") +
  labs(title = "Figure 4C: Price Distribution by Clarity Grade", x = NULL, y = "Price (USD)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")

grid.arrange(p5, p6, p7, ncol = 1)

# 5. Carat vs Price faceted by Cut — interaction visual -------------------
ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = carat, y = price, color = cut)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.07, size = 0.5) +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.9) +
  facet_wrap(~cut, nrow = 1) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = dollar_format()) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "RdYlBu") +
  labs(title = "Figure 5: Carat-Price Relationship Conditioned on Cut Grade", x = "Carat Weight", y = "Price (USD)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + theme(legend.position = "none")

# 6. Residual variance by carat — motivates heteroscedasticity tests ------
model_prelim <- lm(price ~ carat + as.integer(cut) + as.integer(color) + as.integer(clarity), data = Diamond)
Diamond$resid_sq <- residuals(model_prelim)^2

ggplot(Diamond, aes(x = carat, y = sqrt(abs(residuals(model_prelim))))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.07, size = 0.5, color = "#2C7BB6") +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", color = "#D7191C", se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Figure 6: Residual Scale-Location Plot", x = "Carat Weight", y = expression(sqrt("|Residuals|"))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)


```



```{r}
# Data Initialization -----------------------------------------------------

library(tidyquant)
library(dplyr)
library(reshape2)
library(forecast)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(randomForest)

Diamond <- read_csv("diamonds.csv")

Diamond$cut <- as.factor(Diamond$cut)
Diamond$color <- as.factor(Diamond$color)
Diamond$clarity <- as.factor(Diamond$clarity)

# Part a ------------------------------------------------------------------

model1 <- lm(price ~ ., Diamond)
summary(model1)

# Part b ------------------------------------------------------------------

regtree <- rpart(price ~ .,
                 data = Diamond[,c(5,7)],
                 control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 2),
                 method = "anova")

rpart.plot(regtree, digits = -1)

Diamond$widthCat <- ifelse(Diamond$width<6,1,
                           ifelse(Diamond$width>=7,3,2))

model1 <- lm(price ~ ., Diamond[,-7])
summary(model1)

# Part c ------------------------------------------------------------------

Diamond <- arrange(Diamond, desc(price))
Top5Actual <- head(Diamond, 5)
Bottom5Actual <- tail(Diamond, 5)

LimitedDiamond<- aggregate(price ~ weight + cut + color + clarity, 
                           Diamond, 
                           FUN = mean)

LimitedDiamond <- arrange(LimitedDiamond, desc(price))
Top5Average <- head(LimitedDiamond, 5)
Bottom5Average <- tail(LimitedDiamond, 5)

rf <- randomForest(price ~ weight + cut + color + clarity,
                   data = Diamond, 
                   ntree = 200,
                   mtry = 4, 
                   nodesize = 500, 
                   importance = TRUE)

combinations <- expand.grid(
  weight = unique(Diamond$weight),
  cut = unique(Diamond$cut),
  color = unique(Diamond$color),
  clarity = unique(Diamond$clarity)
)

combinations$predict <- predict(rf, combinations)

combinations <- arrange(combinations, desc(predict))
Top5 <- head(combinations, 5)
Bottom5 <- tail(combinations, 5)

# Bagging and Boosting---------------------------------------------------

library(adabag)
library(rpart)
library(caret)
library(forecast)
library(ipred)
library(gbm)
library(randomForest)
set.seed(1)

diamonds.df <- read.csv("diamonds.csv")

# transform cut, color, and clarity into categorical variable
diamonds.df$cut <- as.factor(diamonds.df$cut)
diamonds.df$color <- as.factor(diamonds.df$color)
diamonds.df$clarity <- as.factor(diamonds.df$clarity)

# partition the data
train.index <- sample(c(1:dim(diamonds.df)[1]), dim(diamonds.df)[1]*0.7)
train.df <- diamonds.df[train.index, ]
valid.df <- diamonds.df[-train.index, ]

# single tree
tr <- rpart(price ~ ., data = train.df)
valid.df$tree <- predict(tr, valid.df[,-5])

# Random forest

rf <- randomForest(price ~ ., 
                   ntree = 200,
                   mtry = 4, 
                   nodesize = 500,
                   data = train.df)

# Predict prices for the validation dataset using random forest
valid.df$forest <- predict(rf, valid.df[, -c(5,9)])

# Bagging
bagged_model <- bagging(price ~ ., data = train.df)

# Predict prices for the validation dataset using bagged model
valid.df$bag <- predict(bagged_model, valid.df[, -c(5,9,10)])

# Boosting
boosted_model <- gbm(price ~ ., data = train.df)

# Predict prices for the validation dataset using boosted model
valid.df$boost <- predict(boosted_model, valid.df[, -c(5,9,10,11)])

# Compare model performance

accuracy(valid.df$tree, valid.df$price)
accuracy(valid.df$forest, valid.df$price)
accuracy(valid.df$bag, valid.df$price)
accuracy(valid.df$boost, valid.df$price)

```


```{r, warning=FALSE}
# 0. Setup and Data Initialization ----------------------------------------
library(tidyquant)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(lmtest)    # For heteroscedasticity tests
library(sandwich)  # For robust standard errors
library(rpart)
library(rpart.plot)
library(randomForest)
library(ipred)     # For bagging
library(gbm)       # For boosting
library(forecast)  # For accuracy metrics

set.seed(42) # Ensure full reproducibility

# Load data
Diamond <- read_csv("diamonds.csv")

# Encode categorical factors
Diamond$cut     <- factor(Diamond$cut, levels = c("Fair","Good","Very Good","Premium","Ideal"))
Diamond$color   <- factor(Diamond$color, levels = c("J","I","H","G","F","E","D"))
Diamond$clarity <- factor(Diamond$clarity, levels = c("I1","SI2","SI1","VS2","VS1","VVS2","VVS1","IF"))

# Partition the data (70% Training, 30% Test)
train_index <- sample(seq_len(nrow(Diamond)), size = 0.7 * nrow(Diamond))
train_df <- Diamond[train_index, ]
test_df  <- Diamond[-train_index, ]

# 1. Parametric OLS Models (Trained on 70% split) -------------------------

# Model 1: Baseline Linear (Integer encoding)
model1 <- lm(price ~ carat + as.integer(cut) + as.integer(color) + as.integer(clarity) + 
               length + width + depth, data = train_df)

# Model 2: Log-Linear Baseline
model2 <- lm(log(price) ~ carat + as.integer(cut) + as.integer(color) + as.integer(clarity) + 
               length + width + depth, data = train_df)

# Model 3: Dummy Variables
model3 <- lm(log(price) ~ carat + cut + color + clarity + length + width + depth, data = train_df)

# Model 4: Carat x Cut Interaction
model4 <- lm(log(price) ~ carat * cut + color + clarity + length + width + depth, data = train_df)

# Model 5: Carat x Clarity Interaction
model5 <- lm(log(price) ~ carat * clarity + cut + color + length + width + depth, data = train_df)


# 2. Heteroscedasticity Diagnostics & Remedies (Section V) ----------------

# Breusch-Pagan Test (Studentized by default in bptest)
bp_test <- bptest(model3)
print(bp_test)

# Goldfeld-Quandt Test (Sorting by Carat)
gq_test <- gqtest(model3, order.by = ~carat, data = train_df)
print(gq_test)

# Remediation: Heteroscedasticity-Consistent (HC3) Standard Errors
model3_robust <- coeftest(model3, vcov = vcovHC(model3, type = "HC3"))
# Note: Use summary(model1), summary(model3), or print(model3_robust) in your console to get coefficient tables for the paper.


# 3. Non-Parametric Machine Learning Models -------------------------------

# A. Regression Tree (CART)
tree_model <- rpart(price ~ carat + cut + color + clarity + length + width + depth, 
                    data = train_df, method = "anova", control = rpart.control(maxdepth = 4))
test_df$pred_tree <- predict(tree_model, test_df)

# B. Bagging
bag_model <- bagging(price ~ carat + cut + color + clarity + length + width + depth, 
                     data = train_df, nbagg = 50)
test_df$pred_bag <- predict(bag_model, test_df)

# C. Random Forest
rf_model <- randomForest(price ~ carat + cut + color + clarity + length + width + depth, 
                         data = train_df, ntree = 200, mtry = 4, nodesize = 500, importance = TRUE)
test_df$pred_rf <- predict(rf_model, test_df)

# D. Gradient Boosting
boost_model <- gbm(price ~ carat + cut + color + clarity + length + width + depth, 
                   data = train_df, distribution = "gaussian", n.trees = 200, interaction.depth = 4, shrinkage = 0.1)
test_df$pred_boost <- predict(boost_model, test_df, n.trees = 200)


# 4. Model Performance Evaluation (Test Set) ------------------------------

# A. OLS Predictions (Requires exponentiating Models 3, 4, and 5 to get dollars)
test_df$pred_m1 <- predict(model1, test_df)
test_df$pred_m3 <- exp(predict(model3, test_df))
test_df$pred_m4 <- exp(predict(model4, test_df))
test_df$pred_m5 <- exp(predict(model5, test_df))

cat("\n--- Out-of-Sample Accuracy: Parametric Models ---\n")
cat("Model 1 (Baseline Linear):\n")
print(accuracy(test_df$pred_m1, test_df$price))

cat("\nModel 3 (Dummy Variables):\n")
print(accuracy(test_df$pred_m3, test_df$price))

cat("\nModel 4 (Carat x Cut):\n")
print(accuracy(test_df$pred_m4, test_df$price))

cat("\nModel 5 (Carat x Clarity):\n")
print(accuracy(test_df$pred_m5, test_df$price))

# B. ML Predictions
cat("\n--- Out-of-Sample Accuracy: Non-Parametric Models ---\n")
cat("Regression Tree:\n")
print(accuracy(test_df$pred_tree, test_df$price))

cat("\nBagging:\n")
print(accuracy(test_df$pred_bag, test_df$price))

cat("\nRandom Forest:\n")
print(accuracy(test_df$pred_rf, test_df$price))

cat("\nGradient Boosting:\n")
print(accuracy(test_df$pred_boost, test_df$price))
```
